Subject: Re: Performance SLOs  Context window & latency impact (FinCo)

Hi John  great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery + next steps so we have alignment on perf targets and what we need to validate: 

1) SLA targets you mentioned
 - P95 latency target: <= 250 ms for typical responses (avg output ~150-300 tokens)
 - 99th percentile: tolerance up to 500 ms for peak loads
 - Throughput: sustained 150 req/s, spiking to 300 req/s for 30s bursts
 - Concurrency target: ~12-16 concurrent requests
 - Streaming required for progressive responses (chunked tokens every ~50ms preferred)

2) Context window and token assumptions
 - Input/context window: up to 8k tokens (mostly long user history + doc context)
 - Output max: 1k tokens for longer summaries/explanations
 - Typical request mix: 60% short (<=256 input tokens), 30% medium (256-2048), 10% long (>2048)

3) Key tradeoffs we discussed
 - Larger context windows increase KV cache pressure and can bump per-token latency; we typically see 10-30% extra end-to-end latency when going from 2k->8k tokens for generation-heavy calls.
 - Streaming mitigates perceived latency for end users, but requires the model/runtime to expose incremental decode with small chunk sizes.
 - Batching helps throughput/cost but increases tail latency if misconfigured with low concurrency.

Immediate asks / next steps:
 - Can you confirm the expected percent of long-context requests ( >4k tokens ) in production?
 - Please share a representative payload sample (redacted) so we can run a benchmark with your average prompt shapes.
 - We will run an initial smoke perf test against a comparable open model/config and return a short runbook + latency report (attached).
 - Proposed slot: Wed 5/5 10:00am PT for a live perf run and go/no-go.

Attachments: redwood_test-harness-runbook.md (smoke test steps), finco_latency_test_results_v1.pdf (initial baseline)

Thanks  I looped Rachel and David on logistics. Rachel, can you own the test run and coordinate infra access? David, heads-up on potential dedicated pool sizing if numbers scale.

Best,

- We have an internal policy that any service giving responses to customers must keep 99th percentile under 600ms; can you advise how Redwood approaches tail latency guarantees and fallbacks?

John  great questions. Short answers and what we'll validate in the smoke run: 

- Streaming: configurable. We expose both token-count and time-based flush. Default is token-chunking at 64 tokens, but you can request smaller chunk sizes (e.g., 8-16 tokens) or a time cadence (e.g., flush every 50ms). We'll include an example request in the runbook.

- Example latency numbers (baseline synthetic from our test harness on similar GPU class):
   * 2k context + 256 output: p95 ~ 120-160 ms
   * 8k context + 1k output: p95 ~ 380-480 ms (this aligns with the 10-30% increase depending on model variant and quantization)
   * Streaming first-byte latency can be ~40-80 ms with aggressive small-chunk config

- Tail guarantees & fallbacks: for Hosted customers we provide routing to lower-latency variants and automatic fallback to smaller-model configs. For Dedicated/Private we can support SLA tiers with reserved capacity; we'll capture a recommended Dedicated pool size if your sustained 150 req/s and concurrency 16 numbers hold.

What we'll run in Wed's smoke test:
 - 10-minute ramp to 150 req/s sustained, 30s burst to 300 req/s
 - Mix matching your payload distribution (short/medium/long)
 - Measure p50/p95/p99 for both end-to-end and decode (streaming) first-byte
 - Verify chunking configs (8/16/64 token flush) impact on perceived latency

I've attached the initial baseline run (finco_latency_test_results_v1.pdf) and the test-harness runbook in Drive: https://drive.google.com/finco-perf-harness

Action items: please upload the sample payloads and any auth details for the test stage (API key or temporary access) to the Drive link. We'll share results and a recommended capacity map after the run.

Best,
Marissa
